lines.en: I’ve noticed lately that I’ve been running out of thoughts, which is odd because I didn’t really think that was possible.
I guess that is a thought too, though. So here’s hoping I’m wrong and that it’s just the melancholy setting in again.
Whatever the case, I don’t have any plans this afternoon. But none of the girls have school today, so I’m sure one of them will find me soon enough.

And, if that’s not the case, I’m sure there’s a bridge nearby I can either throw myself off of or masturbate beneath because those are really the only two compulsions that govern my existence at this point.
Oh, I guess there’s a third one now too.
I’m just not sure how I’d be able to move somewhere colder when none of us are ever getting out of here.
My phone goes off and, as if instinctive (because it basically is by now), I snatch it out of my pocket with amazing deftness that would make even mantis shrimp jealous.
(That last line makes more sense if you know about mantis shrimp).
: Hello?
: Good afternoon, Sensei.
: Jessica?
: Yes. It is me, Jessica.
: That’s good. I was worried for a second that Touka might be calling me. I can’t stand that girl.
: Oh? And why is that?
: She just has so much money and hasn’t cured world hunger yet. She’s clearly a bad person.
: I’m sure she’s trying. And I’m sure you’re not much better in the grand scheme of things. So perhaps you should stop taking so much advantage of her?
: She’s actually one of the few I haven’t taken advantage of yet, so I’m not sure where this is coming from.
: Not sexually. But I’m sure you’ve taken advantage of things she’s given you. Large things. That many people would do many things to have.
: I’m confused because it sounds to me like you’re talking about her breasts and you just said it wasn’t sexual.
: Hah...I’m talking about your apartment. Do you even use it? Like...at all?
: Oh.
: Uhh...yeah. Sometimes.
: When was the last time?
: I’m actually there right now.
: How peculiar. Because that’s where I am right now and I don’t see you.
: What? Why are you in my apartment?
: Probably because I’m a bad person. I needed somewhere to not solve world hunger.
: I think this probably goes against some sort of lease agreement.
: Tell me, if you don’t intend to ever use this space for whatever God-awful reasons I imagined you would have when I gifted it to you, would you mind if I re-gifted it?
: To who? Tsukasa already has one. She can’t have mine as well. I don’t care how many times she’s asked.
: I was thinking more along the lines of a personal gift to myself. The rest of the rooms have already been rented out, you see.
: Have they? Also, don’t you have like ten bedrooms? What do you need my apartment for?
: What do you need your apartment for? Because it doesn’t seem like very much when I needed to have the place dusted just last month.
: Last month? Just how often have you been going there?
: Enough to warrant having it dusted.
: Probably just a coincidence. You see, I’m on my way to the apartment right now, actually.
: Oh? Do you remember how to get here or would you like me to send you the address?
: I remember how to get there because I’m there all the time.
: Why are you keeping up this lie despite me having already claimed your bed?
: You’re in my bed?
: Chances are, I’ve slept in it more than you have.
: I bet I’ve had more sex in it.
: Cute. Is that supposed to make me jealous?
: Did it?
: A little.
: Nice.
: Are you actually coming?
: I mean, I don’t really have anything else going on. Might as well.
: Yasu’s here too. Do you mind?
: Stop turning my bachelor pad into a daycare center. There had to be something in the lease agreement about this as well.
: Why do you keep pretending you were involved in some sort of leasing process? Also, could you stop at the store and pick something up for me? Your refrigerator needs to be restocked.
: For...me? Or for you?
: Can you pick something up or not? I need to know if I should make another call or not.
: Yes, Touka. I can pick up condoms for you.
: I don’t believe those go in the refrigerator.
: What? Of course they do. That’s how you prevent the spermicide from going bad.
: Really? I had no idea. I suppose that makes sense, though.
: Perfect sense. So what brand do you want? Your options are limited.
: To what, exactly?
: None because I refuse to wear them now that Makoto doesn’t make me anymore. See you soon.
: Two bottles of barley tea, some chocolate for Yasu, and one of the premium ikura onigiri for me, please. Thank you.
: Sensei?
: Got it. I’ll be there in half an hour.
: That seems quite long for someone who was already on the way.
: Yeah, well, I’m quite a long guy.
: What?
: ...Sensei?
: What an odd line to hang up on.
: What’d he say, Touka? Is he going to the store for us?
: I’m not sure. He merely said he was a “long guy” and hung up the phone.
: Like his height? Or his sex organ? Because both are true, I think.
: Please don’t say “sex organ,” Yasu. It’s unbecoming.
: Oh, it be coming, alright.
: Did...did you just make a sex joke?
: The Emerald Guardian and Kendo Princess introduced me to comedy as part of the manga club! I’m still learning, though.
: That was actually quite good. Keep it up, Yasu. I’m very proud of you.
: Yay! Praise be! I have acquired humor!
: Just don’t acquire too much. I’m not fond of...drastic change.
: Okay. Two bottles of barley tea, some chocolate for Yasu, and a bunch of condoms for Touka’s secret gangbang party later. That was everything, right?
: My onigiri?
: They were out. Just eat some of the condoms instead. You can ingest the flavored kind.
: Of course. I mean, what other reason would there be to flavor them in the first place?
: Just make sure to refrigerate them afterward.
: For the spermicide, yes. I remember.
: Hi, Sensei. I’m sorry I made you and Ayane very sad during Christmalloween.
: I have reflected on my actions since then and have reminded myself of why I should never talk to anyone about anything other than God. Praise be.
: You don’t need to apologize, Yasu. Everything makes me sad. Don’t take it personally.
: I have to say, Sensei, I’m surprised you came.
: Did you buy me a rug? That was not here last time.
: Another gift. You’re welcome.
: Stop giving me things. Especially without informing me about it until way after the fact.
: It’s for my own benefit as well if that makes you feel any better. You don’t mind if I continue to stay here, do you?
: Uhh...why? You have the manor and your dorm.
: It’s just easier to get to the manor from here is all. And I like how...quaint it is. Plus, being here allows me to supervise what goes on in the apartment better than I can elsewhere.
: Touka also says that she likes how the bed smells like you.
: Wha...no I didn’t! I’ve never said that!
: Heheh...maybe it was just me then. I like it too. Sensei smells good.
: He just smells like...man!
: Mmm...man smell.
: Care to explain what’s going on here, Touka?
: I’m honestly not sure if I can...
Seeing as I plan on staying here for a while and that I’m not actively having sex with either of these girls, our options when it comes to what to do are somewhat limited.
Refusing to ever lead, I let Touka take the reins as she’s far more experienced. And yes, that was a horse joke.
Anyway, she takes it upon herself to put a movie on and, before I know it, the three of us are seated in front of the TV and watching-
: Saw III?
: This is another scary movie, isn’t it? You know I’m not supposed to watch them, Touka. They make the voices come back, but they’re always bad ones instead. I don’t like it.
: You’ll be fine, Yasu. It’s all just special effects. In fact, I’d wager no real pigs were harmed at all. Just don’t quote me on that.
: I feel like I shouldn’t watch this without seeing the first two beforehand.
: You really haven’t seen this? But you’re so old.
: Thank you, Touka. I appreciate that.
: Who’s Touka? My name is Jessica.
: Then thank you, Jessica. I appreciate you pointing out my age after inviting me to hang out with you guys.
: Tell me when the movie is over so I can open my eyes again...
: Age makes little difference to me, Sensei. Girls of my status are typically betrothed by this age.
: And most of us don’t put up a fight even if the husbands selected by our families are older than even you.
: On that note, can you tell me how old your mom is? Because she definitely won’t.
: Oh, of course. She’s-
: Huh.
: How old is she?
: Is it over yet?...
The three of us proceed to sit there, watching the movie in silence as Touka presumably tries to figure out how old her mother is.
Well, two of us are watching the movie. One of us has their eyes closed. But, to be fair, she’s more accustomed than any of us to being blind, so this is probably fine.
Oh. This is happening too.
And quite randomly at that.
I don’t know where Touka got the idea that she could just hold my hand like this, nor do I think she’d be able to comprehend that it’s a bigger step than even sex for me, but...it’s happening.
I’ve gotta admit, though. The non-chalantness of it all was rather smooth. So smooth that I don’t think even Yasu’s noticed.
Nevermind. She’s definitely noticed.
Either that or she’s just staring at Touka’s boobs, which, fair.
: I can’t remember — do you enjoy horror movies, Sensei?
: They’re fine. I just feel like I’ve built up a bit of a tolerance to them given that I live in one.
: So, if you were to choose a favorite subgenre or even just a style, what would it be?
: I think you should go first since you clearly know more about this subject than me.
: Hmm...that’s a rather difficult question, I feel.

: I’ve found I typically enjoy Asian horror the most. There’s something about the way Japanese and Korean films in particular provide subtle background details that I believe adds a great deal to the unsettling atmosphere of a scene as a whole.
: Even more so in scenes that seem otherwise normal and tonally light. Because, just like in reality, it’s what lies beneath the surface that is normally the most disturbing.
: Do you have any examples of that?
: Why, yes. There’s this man I know who presents himself as a regular teacher when, in all actuality, he’s an incorrigible monster feasting on the flesh of teenage girls as if it gives him life.
: Yet here you are holding his hand.
: Why, yes. But I like horror.
: And I could see myself falling for a monster under the right circumstances. Does that make me strange, Sensei?
: You were strange long before this reveal, Touka.
: I don’t like monsters. The last one I saw had a TV on his shoulder and a baby in his stomach.
: What? What is that creature from? I haven’t heard of this one at all.
: I’m pretty sure she’s talking about Wilford Blackhole Hands.
: You know Wilford?! I don’t like him! He’s scary! And always trying to slap me!
: Why is it that both of you know of this Wilford when I am the horror enthusiast here?
: You’re probably better off not knowing, Touka. You might fall for him.
: Why do you know Wilford? Did you go to the shrine? You shouldn’t go there. It’s bad.
: Why were you there if it’s so bad?
: I didn’t know what to do when all the noises stopped, so I had to resort to drastic measures. But I have learned my lesson...
: I don’t want to see Wilford anymore...
: Well, now I just feel like I must.
We wind up talking through the rest of the movie, which doesn’t seem to bother Touka as much as I thought it would. But I also imagine she’s seen it a million times before, so there’s that too.
The sun has gone down by the time the credits finish rolling. And seeing as I am now hungry and Touka is without her onigiri, the two of us get up to go find something to eat.
Yasu, on the other hand, decides against joining us. For reasons I’m sure she will very adequately explain in the moments to come.
: (Airplane noises)
: What?
: Ack..sorry...I think I swallowed another Yasu.
: Oh no. There are more?
: You sure you don’t want to come out with us? I can promise we won’t go to McDonald’s this time.
: As if I’d ever let you drag me into that establishment in the first place.
: I’m fine...I’m not very hungry. And I have the chocolate you bought me in case that changes.
: Also, the likelihood of Touka receiving your light goes way up if I am not around to ruin things! And I want to save her most, so this is important to me!
: What? Don’t just look at me like that after she blatantly alludes to us having sex.
: I mean, I did hold your hand. And I assumed that was a bigger step for you, so.
: You bitch. You did comprehend it after all.
: Aww, were you inner-monologuing about me? That’s so sweet. I’m never washing this hand again. Which is a big deal when I wash my hands at least twenty times a day.
: That’s way too many times.
: Maybe I just have some very unsightly habits I’ll never tell you about.
: Jesus, why are you so hot?
: Sh...Should I close my eyes again?...
: No, Yasu. That won’t be necessary. We’ll get out of your hair.
: I’m not sure when we’ll be back, though, so make sure to take your medicine when the alarm goes off. Before your bath. I don’t want you almost drowning again.
: I’ll try my best, Touka. And thank you again for the chocolate, Sensei.
: Please be gentle with Touka’s body since you are such a long guy.
: I sure am, Yasu. I sure am.
Having sufficiently navigated whatever just happened, Touka and I exit the apartment and head for the subway.
